subject: chemistry
title: Half-Life Horizon: First-Order Reactions
welcome_lead: Track the steady halving rhythm of first-order kinetics.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on first-order half-life and rate analysis.
final_note: You've timed the universe one half-life at a time.

concepts.def: Time for [A] to fall to half its value.
Graph used to find order and k.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Constant t½ -> first order. t½ proportional to 1/[A0] -> second order. t½ proportional to [A0] -> zero order.

Read three successive half-lives off a concentration-time curve to test.

k = ln 2 / t½ = 0.693 / t½. Units: s^-1.

Alternative: gradient of ln[A] vs t plot is -k, intercept is ln[A0].

A first-order decay with t½ = 100 s has k = 0.693/100 = 6.93e-3 s^-1. After 300 s (3 half-lives), [A] = [A0]/8.

Used in radioactive decay, pharmacokinetics and enzyme-saturated reactions (zero order in substrate).

numericals.q: t½ = 200 s for first order. k (s^-1) to 3 sf?

free_texts.q: Word meaning time for concentration to halve.
